sentences.text: Kansajsuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.
The genus is based on a single fossil specimen, a right premaxilla from the tip of the snout.
Additional fossils assigned to the genus include vertebrae and bony armor.
The animal was estimated to be between 5 and 7 meters long.
Kansajsuchus was described in 1975 by Mikhail Efimov.
The genus is classified within the family Goniopholididae.
A 2019 study by Kuzmin et al. confirmed that Kansajsuchus belongs to the family Paralligatoridae.
The animal lived from the Cenomanian to the Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
Fossils were found in the lower Santonian-age Upper Cretaceous Yalovach Svita in the Fergana Basin of Tajikistan.
